notes.title: Happy Halloween: Papercraft Jack fights his way through Paper Cut Mansion! 🎃
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36104412/ce65ca467031764d4977436db4c5eafdda6b54ec.jpg[/img]

Pre-Halloween greetings, friends!

[b]First of all:[/b] Thank you so much, folks! Each and everyone of you who enjoys Jack's adventure! I really appreciate that. ❤️

I don't know about you, but I am a sucker for great and creative artstyle. Oh, and for roguelites. And for pumpkins of course. And that's what makes [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1004370/Paper_Cut_Mansion/][b]Paper Cut Mansion[/b][/url] a perfect fit.

You play as police detective Toby, who investigates an old, and spooky mansion, that is a pleasantly reminiscence of Alfred Hitchcock's Psycho. The goal is to find out the secret of the mansion, and as it should be for a roguelite, it takes several attempts to do so, during which permanent equipment is collected.

I really like this kind of game, and that's why I've decided to team up with the devs and we worked together to have an awesome [b]Pumpkin Jack[/b] costume in [b]Paper Cut Mansion[/b]! So, get the burning pumpkin on Toby's head and enjoy the spooky, halloweenish roguelite mood!

All the best and stay healthy everyone!
Nicolas

notes.title: Mark Hamill To Host ‘Thunderful World’ Digital Showcase on November 10th
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37569367/892bc383a39eb0b46c5b4b09af85c4f9f1be9298.jpg[/img]

Hey friends,

we have some awesome news, which we can finally share with you today: We - that's Thunderful Games - welcome all of you to the premiere of our very first digital games showcase ‘[b]Thunderful World[/b]’! ːsteamhappyː

Find out more in the following press release:


[i][b]Gothenburg, Sweden - October 28th, 2021[/b] - International developer and publisher Thunderful Games, creator of the multi-award winning and multi-million selling SteamWorld franchise, is welcoming everyone to a new digital games showcase, ‘[b]Thunderful World[/b]’. The event will be taking place on [b]November 10th at 11am PT / 2pm ET / 7pm GMT / 8pm CET[/b], hosted by Hollywood and pop culture icon [b]Mark Hamill[/b]. Tune in to the livestream on Twitch, YouTube and the [url=https://thunderful.world/][b]thunderful.world[/b][/url] website.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37569367/8a01bc9ec10d1ba6e674354314fd34accd1fbb51.png[/img]

Tune in to see Mark delight us with a ton of exciting new game reveals and announcements from Thunderful. The event will deliver updates on exciting upcoming titles including the surprise indie hit of Summer Game Fest, [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1608230/Planet_of_Lana/][b]Planet of Lana[/b][/url]. There will also be more news on Thunderful titles like [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1608550/Firegirl_Hack_n_Splash_Rescue/][b]Firegirl[/b][/url], [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1726120/Cursed_to_Golf/][b]Cursed to Golf[/b][/url], [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1315610/Source_of_Madness/][b]Source of Madness[/b][/url], [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1276660/Tinkertown/][b]Tinkertown[/b][/url] and [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1158890/White_Shadows/][b]White Shadows[/b][/url]. 

Alongside Mark’s headline hosting role, the event will also feature appearances from Thunderful Group CEO Brjánn Sigurgeirsson, Corporate Vice President at Xbox Sarah Bond, plus a few other surprise industry partners.

Thunderful is proud to be partnering with Xbox and The MIX for Thunderful World. To sign up for the event and be the first to know all the important information ahead of the show on [b]November 10th[/b], head over to [url=https://thunderful.world/][b]thunderful.world[/b][/url]. As your one stop shop for all things Thunderful World, the website will be updated with new announcements and reveals as the event unfolds.[/i]


Stay tuned and tune in on Nov 10th - see you all in the event!
Your Thunderful Games-Team

notes.title: Version 1.3.8 is now live! Also, Steam Trading Cards incoming! 🎃
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36104412/61bde0f69f41b6ce742b5ac47719e9a7aba1b746.jpg[/img]

Spooky scary greetings, friends!

Folks, I am still totally blown away by the overwhelmingly positive feedback I received since the launch of the game – and the constructive suggestions, of course. So, this new update for Pumpkin Jack (1.3.8) is mainly based on the feedback I received from the community! 

[b]And this is what the new update brings to of you all:[/b]

[list]
[*] Added a FOV parameter to the video options
[*] Added HDR support to the video options (only effective for HDR compatible displays)
[*] Added Portuguese - Brazil language to Pumpkin Jack
[*] Added a new timer mode for speedrunner: The full game timer
- This mode enables you to have a timer that takes previous levels in considerations, and give a clean timer for completing the full game from A to Z
- When this mode is enabled, ending a level will put you at the beginning of the next one, no matter if you had a save in this level or not
[/list]
[list]
[*] Fixed a bug where achievements didn’t unlocked properly on level 1
[*] Fixed the speedrun timer look
[*] Fixed a bug where the timer was still counting during mini-game cutscenes
[*] Fixed a bug where the continue button was loading the final boss scene, even if there was no save in level 6
[*] Fixed a bug where opening level 6 from the level selector was opening the final boss scene, even if it was already done. This was blocking people from replaying the level 6 for collection purpose.
[/list]

[b]Oh, and I almost forgot:[/b] From now on the Steam Trading Cards for [b]Pumpkin Jack[/b] are also available! Have fun collecting them!

Thank you all very, very much for your ongoing feedback and support - it's really appreciated! ❤️

All the best and stay healthy everyone!
Nicolas

notes.title: Pumpkin Jack supports Ray Tracing and DLSS! 🎃
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36104412/afe7183443714442d1ba4711fc0f7c653c644046.jpg[/img]

Spooky scary greetings, friends!

When I was younger, I played a lot of games on my computer and very often saw a green logo a lot of you might know already: "Nvidia, the way it's meant to be played". [b]Nvidia[/b]. For me, it was just a big brand producing graphic cards for gamers and doing some programming stuff, but I didn't know exactly what that was. I just knew it was BIG! For me it was not even possible to think about working with Nvidia. A big dream for an 18 year old boy…

But that's the thing with dreams, sometimes they come true: A few month ago, thanks to [b]Pumpkin Jack[/b], I received a request: "Would you like to add Nvidia RTX to Pumpkin Jack?". At this moment I couldn't believe it... Who could have imagined that? Such a big company was interested in my game?!? I said "yes" of course, and so started the process of adding this new technology to my game.

At first, when I received the files I was supposed to use, I couldn't understand anything and almost decided to give it up. But a few weeks later, I had some free time and decided to get my hands REALLY dirty this time. And so, I started to read the full documentation, trying to understand how things work - or don't work. 

[b]So, what is ray tracing anyway? [/b]
"Ray tracing is the holy grail of gaming graphics, simulating the physical behavior of light to bring real-time, cinematic-quality rendering to even the most visually intense games." [i](NVIDIA official website)[/i] 

I first started with adding RTX shadows to [b]Pumpkin Jack[/b]. This was the easiest part, and it took me only a few days. The work was mainly using commands to enable/disable features or tweak some others. I did not have to write any code myself. But the results were pretty nice: 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36104412/973e8f8ed8c79202a4962fba02024d7a0bceb098.jpg[/img]

Now that RTX shadows were working, I moved forward to RTX reflections - for water for example. And this one was hard! I mean VERY HARD! It actually took me a whole month, just for this alone. It was tricky as translucency was not very well supported at the moment. I tried my best, but finally I decided to make opaque water, which at least worked: 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36104412/e18f82395e5213c1b8d13f53119a8c54a9747fef.jpg[/img]

But it was looking strange, a bit flat. And I was simply not satisfied with the result. So, I emailed [b]Nvidia[/b] and asked them how to fix that. They told me that they worked on something very, very new recently and it could make my translucent water work; called Hybrid-Translucency. A few emails later, I got the files and could start working... and... WOW! It was working just fine! And it is looking damn perfect: 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36104412/82c3b2763dd2ee69774387b531fbd859e67dbf62.jpg[/img]

So that's how I implemented Nvidia RTX to [b]Pumpkin Jack[/b] in a nutshell. It was a lot of research work, lot of confusion and trying to make things that are not supposed to work. But with the help of the folks over at [b]Nvidia[/b], I was able to make it. Thank you very much for your support! 

I'm very happy to have RTX working in [b]Pumpkin Jack[/b], especially since it's one of the first cartoon games that uses this technology! I guess it makes [b]Pumpkin Jack[/b] a pioneer in some way. And me as a young developer (23 years is still young, right?) really very proud of my work.

At first, I was afraid and skeptical that the RTX features would not work with the style of [b]Pumpkin Jack[/b], but I think the result speaks for itself:

[previewyoutube=sMM-mJEl_4Y;full][/previewyoutube]

notes.title: From seed to harvest: The ripening process of Pumpkin Jack!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36104412/bc4212a9699879037d387d22a3e467f623c6a0f5.jpg[/img]

Once upon a time in a far away kingdom... I was looking for a game on Steam. Something that would be colourful as well as a single player experience offering a great adventure. Even after weeks of searching I was not able to find what I was looking for.

I am pretty sure that happened because I was unconsciously looking for something being exact like my favorite game of my childhood, Jak & Daxter, which was unfortunately never ported to the PC.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36104412/72abe535a1784ba3cecd081b85cdec84cbdc014f.png[/img]

That was when an idea came to my mind: If the one I am searching for is not available, why not create my own game? I had no idea how easy or hard this would be, I just wanted to do this. So everything started with a simple search on Google: "How to make games". Yeah, it sounds like a cheap cliché, but it was the beginning of a (felt) endlessly long learning process.

At first, I wanted to make a scarecrow that could control crows. True, it's a stereotype. But hey, that’s the way everything began. I learned to create 3D models, made my first scarecrow, taught myself how to animate it and learned how to integrate it into the Unreal Engine. Thanks to modern software we have nowadays, those steps only took me one week! Following that, I created more animations to let the scarecrow attack, and made some monsters to have something for it to attack.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36104412/6ec0a9976255906d5aa572d8d04d51d61cab95a1.png[/img]

A few months later I canceled the project because it felt not good enough. I started all over again with my newly learned skills, and it worked way better! But I canceled it again, remade it, canceled it again, and again, and again... I believe I started and stopped the project six times in total until I was satisfied with what finally laid the foundation for 'Curse of the Scarecrow', what the project was called then!

Two years later I released a first demo on Itch.io. It had gone wild and was much, much more successful than I expected! At this point I started to realize that my little project might have the potential to become something way bigger than what I aimed for initially. I received emails from YouTubers, streamers and even publishers who wanted to help me with the game. This was insane, I just couldn't realize what was happening. But believe me, I was incredibly happy!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36104412/b737117b57aadfb7e385031c92bbe62c41a23cb2.png[/img]

Finally I decided to quit my job (I worked for a French game development studio) and started to work full time on Curse of The Scarecrow. People seemed to like my game, and so did I and wanted to spend more time on it.

I was looking for a publisher and so I wanted to deliver the best game I could, and I decided to cancel the game once again and (you guessed it) re-built it once more. Why again? Because I want to deliver the best possible experience to you players out there! And so, Curse of The Scarecrow died, and Pumpkin Jack emerged.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36104412/4ddb0bdd7985ddb24c09cc218e1840edce9762ef.png[/img]

From that point onwards I had the chance to work with the guys from the German-based publisher Headup, who helped me out and made this game possible. Today it is a huge pleasure and a very huge honor to see my own game, my childhood dream game, on its way to be available very soon on PC and consoles!

I have learned so much on this long journey - professionally, but also personally. Finally, what is the moral of this story with a happy ending? You yourself are responsible for making your dreams come true! Yeah, and that's definitely a good ending, too.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36104412/3ff9cb7b2cdbb803d78a5f4beec8e6b404443e6d.png[/img]
